title: Shikonin Attenuates Liver Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Through Direct Interaction With HMGB1 Protein.
authors: Zhang, Libang; Liu, Fang; Shen, Pingping; Jiang, Xuewa; Raj, Richa; Zhang, Jian; Li, Guolong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究紫草素与HMGB1蛋白的直接结合以减轻肝缺血再灌注损伤，虽涉及蛋白-配体互作和分子动力学模拟，但对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法部分可借鉴。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury represents a critical clinical challenge characterized by excessive inflammation. HMGB1, known as a proinflammatory mediator released after liver IR injury, has been reported to worsen the damage and inflammation via a positive feedback loop. Herein, shikonin has been explored to alleviate hepatic IR injury through direct interaction with HMGB1. METHODS: The ligation on the hilum of the right liver lobe lasted for 90 min and then removed to induce hepatic IR injury in SD rats. Serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) were determined. At the cellular level, HMGB1-induced NO release from RAW264.7 was assessed to test the inhibitory effect of shikonin. The surface plasmon resonance (SPR), saturation transfer difference nuclear magnetic resonance (STD-NMR), and molecular dynamics simulation were employed to study the interaction between shikonin and HMGB1. RESULTS: After administration of shikonin, the degree of liver IR damage in rats was attenuated significantly in a dose-dependent manner. In vitro, shikonin can effectively inhibit HMGB1 activation. Furthermore, mechanistic studies indicated that shikonin could directly bind to HMGB1. The results of (1)H STD-NMR confirmed that shikonin interacted with HMGB1, and multiple protons in shikonin participated in the binding process. Notably, shikonin exhibits a selective binding affinity toward the I122 and L129-bearing region of HMGB1, which were supported by molecular dynamics simulation. CONCLUSION: In general, our results suggest that shikonin is a promising natural candidate that directly targets HMGB1 to exert hepatoprotection for the development of clinical therapeutic anti-IR agents.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：肝脏缺血再灌注（IR）损伤是一种以过度炎症为特征的临床挑战。HMGB1 作为肝脏 IR 损伤后释放的促炎介质，据报道通过正反馈环路加重损伤和炎症。本研究探讨了紫草素（shikonin）通过与 HMGB1 直接相互作用减轻肝脏 IR 损伤的作用。方法：对大鼠右肝叶门部结扎 90 分钟，然后解除结扎以诱导 SD 大鼠肝脏 IR 损伤。测定血清天冬氨酸氨基转移酶（AST）和丙氨酸氨基转移酶（ALT）。在细胞水平上，评估 HMGB1 诱导的 RAW264.7 细胞 NO 释放，以测试紫草素的抑制作用。采用表面等离子体共振（SPR）、饱和转移差谱核磁共振（STD-NMR）和分子动力学模拟研究紫草素与 HMGB1 之间的相互作用。结果：给予紫草素后，大鼠肝脏 IR 损伤程度以剂量依赖性方式显著减轻。体外实验表明，紫草素能有效抑制 HMGB1 激活。此外，机制研究表明紫草素可直接结合 HMGB1。(1)H STD-NMR 结果证实紫草素与 HMGB1 相互作用，且紫草素中多个质子参与结合过程。值得注意的是，紫草素对 HMGB1 的 I122 和 L129 所在区域表现出选择性结合亲和力，这一结果得到分子动力学模拟的支持。结论：总体而言，我们的结果表明紫草素是一种有前景的天然候选药物，通过直接靶向 HMGB1 发挥肝脏保护作用，为开发临床治疗性抗 IR 药物提供基础。
